Labour study · Skill → value → obligation

What Fashion Owes Its Craftspeople

Fashion owes craftspeople more than romantic visibility: lawful and timely pay, safe conditions, credible credit, worker voice, remedy, preserved knowledge, and limits on extraction—specified for the actual relationship and jurisdiction.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

A gown’s beadwork, structure, finishing, dye, embroidery, cutting, pressing, and repair can be visible while the people responsible remain absent from the surviving record. The House of Worth ball gown preserves materials and house attribution; it cannot, by itself, establish who performed each task or under what conditions. That absence must not be filled with invented names.

Official labor sources narrow what can responsibly be claimed. U.S. Department of Labor guidance addresses covered garment-industry compliance; ILO research examines how purchasing practices, wages, working conditions, and gendered occupational structures operate in particular supply-chain contexts. None supplies a universal contract. Together they make one principle unavoidable: admiration for craft cannot substitute for evidence about pay, conditions, power, and remedy.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · NAME

Can the worker choose to be credited?

Build role-level credits with consent: cutter, embroiderer, weaver, dyer, machinist, finisher, presser, sample maker, repairer, and others as locally accurate. Protect people where naming creates risk.

PROPOSALS72S76S85

02 · PAY

What commercial decisions reach the workroom?

Trace price, lead time, revisions, cancellations, overtime, payment schedule, subcontracting, and remedy. Purchasing decisions upstream can shape downstream labor outcomes; verify the actual chain.

INFERENCES76S81S86

03 · VOICE

Who can refuse, correct, and report harm?

Document worker-representation and grievance routes, anti-retaliation protections, safety escalation, correction of public credits, and who controls the response. A feedback form without remedy is not voice.

PROPOSALS76S81S87

04 · KNOWLEDGE

What does preservation return?

With consent, preserve process narration, terminology, samples, and contributor authority. Do not convert community knowledge into proprietary house content without permission, attribution, benefit, and cultural review.

PROPOSALS88S10S72

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Publicly naming craft can create recognition, but it may expose workers, simplify collective production, disclose confidential methods, or become reputation-washing. Credits, compensation, safety, bargaining, and cultural authority require separate mechanisms.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Choose one object and list only the roles the evidence supports; label every missing contributor unresolved.
  2. Map price, lead time, change orders, overtime, subcontracting, payment, and remedy through the actual production chain.
  3. Ask workers or representatives which credit, anonymity, archive, and correction options are safe and useful.
  4. Route wage, classification, safety, contract, and cross-border issues to qualified labor counsel and local specialists.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical essay: Beyond the Romance of the Hand
  • Ten-minute labor-and-value film
  • Nine-frame credit-is-not-compensation carousel
  • Five craft-power verticals
  • Craft Obligation Ledger
  • Newsletter, procurement, classroom, and worker-review editions

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Begin at the glittering surface, then trace each verified material and task backward toward price, time, safety, pay, voice, and remedy. Leave unknown workers visibly unnamed rather than fabricating completeness.

02

SHORT 01 — “Credit is not compensation.” Add: compensation is not safety; visibility is not bargaining power; heritage is not consent.

03

SHORT 02 — The purchase-order test: did price, lead time, revisions, and cancellation terms make lawful and safe work possible?

04

CAROUSEL — Nine obligations: identify; consent; contract; pay; time; safety; voice; remedy; preserve. Each frame includes a verification field.

05

AUDIO — A worker-review protocol with interpreter, anonymity, stopping, correction, and publication-consent choices.

06

PROCUREMENT — A pre-order worksheet that routes jurisdiction-specific wage, classification, safety, and contracting questions to qualified local review.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
